setupSteps: Pin: put the selector pin fully into a light plate (Gym 4). Push it all the way in.

Find your lever or pad adjustment. Many machines let you slide the roller pad (a pull-pin or knob) so that, when your legs are straight, it rests just above your ankles (NASM; ExRx). NASM's single-leg page instead describes the pad on the lower calf near the Achilles (heel) tendon, so brands differ; the ankle-pad rule is: just above the ankles, not on the Achilles tendon, not mid-calf.

Lie face down. Put your knees just off the edge of the bench so your knee joint lines up with the machine's pivot (the round hinge at the side; ExRx/Fitwill cue). Many benches have a small bend (hip slope) built in; leave it as built.
Hips and stomach: hips pressed on the pad, hip bones against the bench. Hold the handles (ExRx).
Head: neck relaxed, face looking down at the bench or slightly to one side, in line with the spine (NASM EDGE cue: head in line with the back).

Ankles: roller pad on the back of the heels or just above; toes pointing back and slightly toward the shins (dorsiflexed, "toes pulled toward you"). ExRx notes that pulling the toes up reduces gastrocnemius "active insufficiency" so it can help the curl; a 2023 within-person trial found no clear difference in hamstring EMG between ankle positions, so this is a comfort choice.
Start position: legs straight but not snapped straight (soft knees). If there is a start-position adjustment, set it so the stack hangs without strain.
Pin: put the selector pin fully into a light plate (Gym 4).

Back pad: slide the seat or back pad (usually a lever or pin, often numbered) so your knee joint lines up with the lever's pivot (ExRx: position back of seat so knees are aligned with the fulcrum; Hoist machine guide).
Ankle pad: set the roller on the back of the lower legs just above the ankles (ExRx), not on the Achilles tendon.

Thigh pad: lower it until it rests firmly on the thighs just above the knees, snug but not squeezing (ExRx; University of Western Ontario campus rec equipment guide). It stops your hips and thighs lifting.
Sit: buttocks back against the seat, back against the pad, hands on the handles (ExRx). Put the leg nearer the lever in first (ExRx).

Start position (if adjustable): some machines have 3–5 start positions (Hammer Strength Select lists five). Choose the one where legs are straight, or very slightly bent if your hamstrings feel a hard stretch behind the knee; reduce range if the stretch strains your knees (Hoist guide).
Check for leg length: if the pad sits on your calves or Achilles, shorten the lever or ask staff to show you the adjustment; shorter people often need the seat moved forward.

steps.title: Brace and flatten
steps.action: With legs straight (soft knees), gently tighten your stomach and press your hips into the bench.
steps.feel: Hip bones heavy on the pad; lower back not arched.
steps.visualCheck: Side: back flat, hips on bench, legs almost straight. Front/top: hips level.

steps.title: Curl up
steps.action: Bend your knees to bring the heels toward the buttocks, moving only the lower legs.
steps.feel: Back of thighs working; maybe slight calf effort.
steps.visualCheck: Side: thighs and hips stay down; heels travel in an arc. Front: both legs move together.

steps.title: Squeeze at the top
steps.action: Stop when the heels are near the buttocks or when your hips would start to lift, whichever comes first (NASM single-leg cue: heel up as far as possible without arching or lifting the hips).
steps.feel: Strong hamstring squeeze; no pinch in the lower back.
steps.visualCheck: Side: knee angle about 40–70° (est.), hips still flat.

steps.title: Lower slowly
steps.action: Let the pad return by straightening the knees under control.
steps.feel: Hamstrings stretching and braking the weight.
steps.visualCheck: Side: smooth, no drop; hips stay down.

steps.title: Stop just short of locking
steps.action: Stop with the knees almost straight (NASM: stop just short of full extension to keep tension).
steps.feel: Weight held by muscle, stack not touching.
steps.breathing: Breathe in fully before the next rep.
steps.visualCheck: Side: a small bend visible at the knee.

steps.title: Repeat for the planned reps, then lower the stack slowly until the plates rest silently; sit up and step off
Brace
steps.action: Back against the pad, thigh pad snug, legs straight and soft, tighten your stomach lightly.
steps.feel: Thighs held under the pad, back supported.
steps.visualCheck: Side: upright back, thighs level or slightly sloping, ankle pad above ankles.

steps.title: Curl down and back
steps.action: Press the roller pad down and back by bending the knees until the lower legs are under the seat line, about 90° or a little more bent (NASM seated start/finish cues use about 90° knee bends).
steps.feel: Back of thighs working; the pad pushing into the calves.
steps.visualCheck: Side: the back stays against the pad; thighs stay pressed under the pad.

steps.title: Squeeze
steps.action: Pause with the knees bent as far as your range allows, hips still.
steps.visualCheck: Side: knee angle about 60–90° (est.); no leaning forward off the back pad.

steps.title: Return slowly
steps.action: Let the legs rise back toward straight, keeping tension.
steps.feel: Stretch behind the thighs and knees.
steps.visualCheck: Side: no jerk; thigh pad holds legs down.

steps.title: Stop just short of locking and repeat. Finish by returning the stack until it rests gently
Curl with one leg while the other rests on the pad or floor (machine permitting)
Keep hips and thighs still; switch legs after the set

commonMistakes.title: Hips lifting off the bench (lying)
commonMistakes.text: Hips lifting off the bench (lying). Why: moves the load onto the lower back and takes work off the hamstrings (Liftosaur; NASM names hip shift as a common mistake). Fix: lighter weight, stop the curl before the hips rise; press hips into the bench. Note: Iron Man magazine allows about an inch of hip rise for full contraction; FitPlate chooses the stricter "hips stay down" because sources agree it reduces back strain.

commonMistakes.title: Arching the lower back
commonMistakes.text: Arching the lower back. Why: the spine takes up the effort instead of the knees (ExRx: keep the torso flat to limit lower back hyperextension). Fix: tighten the stomach, lower the weight, or switch to the seated machine.

commonMistakes.title: Using too much weight and swinging
commonMistakes.text: Using too much weight and swinging. Why: momentum, hip pop and a jerk on the hamstring at the end of range (Fitness Volt; Famme). Fix: weight that allows 10–12 slow reps at about 3 reps in reserve.

commonMistakes.title: Dropping the weight on the way down
commonMistakes.text: Dropping the weight on the way down. Why: loses the controlled stretch under load and can jolt the knees and hamstrings. Fix: 3 seconds down, always.

commonMistakes.title: Misaligned pivot (knee not at the hinge)
commonMistakes.text: Misaligned pivot (knee not at the hinge). Why: the pad slides along your leg and the range shifts (ExRx; Fitwill; Hoist). Fix: re-adjust the seat or lever and note the settings.

commonMistakes.title: Pad on the Achilles tendon or too high on the calf
commonMistakes.text: Pad on the Achilles tendon or too high on the calf. Why: pressure on the tendon, or the pad slips and the lever arm changes. Fix: just above the ankles; ask staff for the adjustment.

commonMistakes.title: Locking out the knees and bouncing at the bottom
commonMistakes.text: Locking out the knees and bouncing at the bottom. Why: transfers the load to the joint and lets momentum do the work. Fix: stop just short of straight and keep tension.

commonMistakes.title: Rushing through half-reps
commonMistakes.text: Rushing through half-reps. Why: less muscle work; for the seated curl in particular the lengthened start is where the benefit lies (Maeo 2021). Fix: use the full comfortable range at a lighter load.

commonMistakes.title: Lifting the thighs off the seat pad (seated)
commonMistakes.text: Lifting the thighs off the seat pad (seated). Why: the thigh pad is not doing its job. Fix: lower the pad firmly onto the thighs and reduce the load.

safetyNotes: Hamstring strain or tear (recent): NHS Wales advises stopping exercise at the first sign of pain in the leg; mild strains settle in a few days, severe ones (pop, can't use the leg) need a GP (nidirect). Return to leg curls only when pain-free; start very light.

Hamstring-graft knee surgery (ACL): published protocols delay resisted hamstring curls for about 6–12 weeks (e.g. Indiana Bone & Joint: none before week 8; Dartmouth: restricted 12 weeks). Follow your surgeon.
Knee problems: use a light load and reduced range; stop if kneecap or joint pain rises.
Lower back problems: prefer the seated version (back supported); on the lying machine, stop if your back arches or you feel pain.
High blood pressure / heart disease: breathe continuously, no straining to failure, rest at least 60 s (est.).

Pregnancy: the face-down lying machine is not suitable once the belly is large; secondary sources say traditional advice (attributed to ACOG) avoids lying flat on the back after the first trimester. Use the seated version and ask your obstetrician.
Larger bodies: check the machine's maximum user weight and whether the bench and pad fit.
